about.title: Montclair Wrongful Death Claims
about.longDescription: When a crash on Central Avenue, Monte Vista Avenue, or along the San Bernardino Freeway takes a loved one's life, the grief is immediate but the legal questions often surface later. San Bernardino County records show Montclair saw 234 injury collisions and 348 people hurt in the most recent final crash year, with one traffic death — a reminder that even a small city carries real risk on its busiest roads, especially during Friday evening hours when traffic peaks. California law gives surviving spouses, domestic partners, and children the first right to bring a wrongful death claim, with other dependents eligible in certain situations. LawProactive is a free connection service, not a law firm, and we don't charge families anything to find an independent attorney who can explain your options. Attorneys in our network work on contingency, meaning there's no fee unless there's a recovery. You deserve time to grieve, not a rushed legal decision, and having someone in your corner from the start can make the road ahead a little clearer.

items.title: Time Limits Matter
items.desc: California generally allows two years from the date of death to file a wrongful death claim, though claims involving a government entity carry a much shorter deadline. Acting sooner preserves evidence and options.

items.title: Only Certain Family Members Can File
items.desc: California law limits who has standing to bring a wrongful death claim, starting with a spouse, domestic partner, or children, with other dependents potentially eligible depending on the family's circumstances. An attorney can clarify who qualifies in your specific situation.

items.title: Recoverable Losses Go Beyond Bills
items.desc: California allows families to seek funeral and burial costs and lost financial support, as well as compensation for the loss of a loved one's love, companionship, and guidance. These claims are civil matters, entirely separate from any criminal case that may also be underway.

items.question: How long do we have to file a wrongful death claim in Montclair?
items.answer: Under California law, the general deadline is two years from the date of death. If a government entity, such as a city or county road authority, may be involved, that deadline is much shorter and requires an earlier claim filing. Because facts vary, it's wise to speak with an attorney as soon as you're able.

items.question: Can we pursue a wrongful death claim even if criminal charges are also filed?
items.answer: Yes. A wrongful death claim is a separate civil action from any criminal prosecution connected to the crash. The outcome of one doesn't determine the outcome of the other, and families can move forward with a civil claim regardless of the criminal case's status.

items.question: Does it matter that the crash happened on a busy Montclair road like Central Avenue or the I-10?
items.answer: Public crash records for Montclair show collisions cluster on corridors like Central Avenue, Monte Vista Avenue, Holt Boulevard, and the I-10 freeway, often around Friday evenings. Where and when a crash happened can affect which agencies or parties may be involved in an investigation, which is something an attorney can look into on your behalf.
